reading.title: Fixing traffic
reading.text: Every big city faces traffic jams, and every mayor promises to solve them. The usual solution has been to build more roads, but research shows that new lanes fill up within a few years. Some cities have tried a different approach. Stockholm introduced a congestion charge in 2006: drivers pay to enter the centre at busy times. Traffic fell by about 20 percent almost overnight. The scheme was unpopular at first, but after a public vote the dispute was resolved and the charge was made permanent. Experts warn, however, that there is no absolute answer: what works in one city may fail in another.

items.s: New roads usually reduce traffic for many years.
